thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU OOM detected during prefill on cluster dedicated-gpu-prod-3. Multiple container restarts observed across nodes 3/7. Auto-escalating to on-call.

alex: I’m on it, paging SRE. Which jobs are hitting this? any obvious client?

maria: Runtime logs show repeated large prefill sequences from a single customer token stream — lots of very long prompts (~200k tokens) triggering early allocation spikes and then CUDA OOM. stack trace snippet below.

maria: ```
2026-03-15T18:10:02Z runtime: prefill starting, input_len=198432
2026-03-15T18:10:03Z cuda: attempt alloc 234MB -> OOM
2026-03-15T18:10:03Z runtime: container restart requested (exit code 137)
2026-03-15T18:10:04Z kubelet: restarting container
```

ryan: Support here — we already have 2 paying customers reporting elevated error rates and timeouts in the last 10m. One flagged as P1 (low-latency inference). They saw 502/503s.

tara: Any correlation with prefill batching params? We pushed a throughput tweak an hour ago.

maria: Not seeing any new deploys except an autoscaler change 2h ago. But these prefill payloads are insane. Their client appears to be sending concatenated transcripts without streaming.

alex: Quick triage plan: (1) stop accepting huge prefill payloads at gateway (reject > 64k tokens), (2) temporarily route long-prefill traffic to cpu-serve or smaller model, (3) tag and cordon affected nodes, (4) notify customers. Who can run the gateway rule?

support-led: I can draft a customer msg once we confirm scope. Which customers affected?

maria: Running query — giving me 90s. Current noisy source: api-key sk-prod-45xxx from acct ACME-Widgets. Also seeing duplicate flows from sk-prod-12yyy.

alex: @deploy-bot can you push a quick runtime guard? Prefer config toggle over full deploy. Add prefill_max_tokens=65536 and reject with 413 + 'prefill too large' for now.

deploy-bot: Received. Preparing canary patch: runtime-config v2026-03-15-hotfix-001. Canary on node dedicated-gpu-prod-3b.

maria: Applying cordon to node dedicated-gpu-prod-3b now and draining pods that frequently restart.

maria: Patch applied to canary node. Observing that new requests with extremely long prefill are now returning 413 at the gateway. No restarts in the canary for the last 3m.

alex: Good. Rolling to remaining nodes in cluster with staggered 30s spacing. Keep an eye for regressions.

ryan: Customer impact update: ACME-Widgets reported 12 failed requests in last 5m. They had a job that retried aggressively; some retries started to hit healthy nodes after patch. Draft message below for review: "We're investigating elevated errors this afternoon caused by very large inputs. We've implemented temporary limits to protect latency. If you need higher limits, please contact support for a dedicated path."

support-led: Draft looks good. Add apology and ETA for follow-up.

maria: After rolling config, container restarts dropped to zero across the cluster. Total restarts before fix: ~38 in 12m; after: 0 in 7m. Memory pressure graphs look much healthier (spike amplitude down 60%).

alex: Action items while incident is active:
- support-led: send initial customer comms and log affected accounts (ACME-Widgets, beta-partner-9).
- eng-runtime (maria): implement long-term mitigation: prefill streaming warnings, better memory reservation, and soft-fail fallback to quantized model.
- infra (alex): run a postmortem and consider autoscaler guardrails to avoid noisy-e2e scale-downs.

maria: Quick mitigation note: we can also enable prefix KV cache trimming for huge prefill so we don't allocate full KV at once. Will prototype tomorrow.

deploy-bot: Canary complete. Hotfix rolled to all nodes in dedicated-gpu-prod cluster. Version v2026-03-15-hotfix-001.

ryan: Sent initial customer emails to affected accounts. Logged as P1 for ACME-Widgets; they acknowledged and asked for timeline.

alex: Handoff — I need to jump to another page. @maria you take post-incident lead. If anything breaks escalate back to me. :hand:

maria: Taking it. I'll run the RCA and schedule follow-ups. Thanks @alex. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated. Severity: Sev2 (partial customer impact).

maria: Preliminary root cause: lack of upper bound on prefill length at gateway + client behavior sending monolithic transcripts. Contributing factor: runtime alloc pattern that tries to reserve full KV memory for prefill instead of streaming/gradual reservation.

support-led: Final note for customer comms: offer a temporary quota override for enterprise customers needing larger contexts and advise best practices: streaming, chunked uploads.

alex: Good job team. We'll keep monitoring for 24h; if no regressions we can close the incident and run a short postmortem doc.

maria: I'll attach logs and graphs to the PM doc and set the postmortem meeting for tomorrow 11:00.

support-led: Closing loop with customers after the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> monitoring. Duration: 00:35:00.
